2.text: were almost starving, when some Tungus who were passing by saw their

3.text: tracks and came to their rescue. Shortly afterwards Father Venedict left the

4.text: Kolyma and went to Yakutsk. I do not think that he will ever come back.

5.text: The journey of Father Venedict is quite remarkable. I do not think, however,

6.text: that he has done much for the spread of the Gospel. When starting on

7.text: his journey, he knew absolutely nothing of the Chukchee language. In his

8.text: camp was a young Russian woman who was married to a Chukchee. This

9.text: woman acted as an interpreter for him. They parted somewhere on the

10.text: Arctic shore. After that he had to give all his attention to the mere neces-

11.text: sities of life and to the continuation of his journey; at least, Kɪlaˊtɪ and the

12.text: other Chukchee said nothing about Venedict’s preaching. On the contrary,

13.text: they related that he was silent for the most part, but all of a sudden began

14.text: to cry “like a little baby.” His trial was too hard.

15.text: The third missionary of this time was Father Michael. This one was

16.text: not a monk. He was a deacon for a long time, and wanted greatly to be

17.text: ordained as a priest. For this purpose he began to visit the Chukchee camps,

18.text: though he was occupied, not with preaching, but with trading. He also tried

19.text: to write a dictionary of the Chukchee language. The people of the Kolyma

20.text: said laughingly, “He writes his dictionary on fawn-skins, and sends it to

21.text: Nishne-Kolymsk by large bagfuls;” and, indeed, there was much truth in this.

22.text: For instance, he brought with him some small pictures representing images

23.text: of the saints, printed on paper, which he received free of cost from Yakutsk.

26.text: At last he was ordained. Then, not needing his dictionary any longer,

27.text: he gave it to me. I have it now among my papers. It is a small quire of

28.text: paper, quite greasy, unbound, and written in pencil. Father Michael’s system

29.text: was the following. He copied all the words from a small printed Russian-

30.text: German dictionary, and then tried to translate them into Chukchee with the

31.text: aid of an interpreter. Among other words translated were “duke,” “governess,”

32.text: etc. Apart from this attempt at scientific work, he knew very little of the

33.text: Chukchee language. He was made Chukchee missionary because at the time

34.text: of his ordination there was no parish unoccupied. He was appointed for work

35.text: among the Reindeer Chukchee to the east of the Kolyma. He made frequent

36.text: journeys among the camps, but chiefly for trading-purposes.

37.text: With such preachers, it is no wonder that most of the Chukchee, with

38.text: the exception of those who live nearest to the Russian settlements, have

39.text: remained until now unbaptized. Even those that have, properly speaking,

40.text: been baptized, cannot be called Christians even in name. Not one of them

41.text: knows so much as the name of Christ. They do not care to remember the

42.text: new Christian names given to them. They live as they have lived, bring
